subject: Ozark Digital - Post-demo architecture checklist & keying options
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jess@ozarkdigital.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Ozark Digital - Post-demo architecture checklist & keying options

Hi Jessica — thanks again for joining the demo today. Quick follow-up with the items we promised to capture so your infra team can review. Summary and suggested next steps below.

Key asks from demo:
- Confirm target volume (QPS / tokens per month) for inference and embeddings. You mentioned ~60M tokens/month for customer-facing features and ~2M embeddings/month for search.
- Verify regulatory constraints (data residency / audit trail) for logs and KV cache retention.
- Decide preferred auth pattern for server-to-Redwood traffic: API keys, OAuth client credentials with short-lived JWTs, or service-account + token exchange.

Suggested architecture for first PoC (low friction, secure):
1) SDK + service account pattern
   - Use a single service account per environment (staging/prod).
   - Exchange long-lived service account credentials for short-lived tokens (30m) inside your token broker.
   - Integrate with your KMS for key storage; rotate the underlying credential quarterly.
2) Scoped API keys for dev / demo
   - Developer keys (scoped, rate-limited) for sandbox; do not use for production.
3) Routing & regions
   - Route EU traffic to eu.redwood.example.net endpoints for data residency.
   - Use smart routing: low-latency for real-time chat, cost-optimized for batch embedding jobs.
4) Embeddings & reranker notes
   - Precompute dense embeddings for static content and store vector index in your current vector DB.
   - Use Redwood rerank endpoint for re-ranking candidate sets (keeps token usage predictable).

Attachments I’m including: redwood-keying-options.pdf (summary of patterns), integration-snippets.zip (SDK quickstart + token-broker sample), and ozark-initial-map.md (checklist).

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm the QPS and compliance constraints by EOD Friday? (These will drive whether we recommend service account + token broker or OAuth.)
- If OK, schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra team and ours next week (I’ll propose slots).

Thanks — Soojin

Thanks, Soojin — good rundown. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volume: The 60M tokens/month is the upper bound for year-1; typical bursts during business hours will be ~500 QPS for text generation. Embeddings peak at ~1800 vectors/hr during ingestion windows.
- Compliance: All inference logs must be retained for 90 days; PII redaction needed at the prompt level (we handle redaction in-app but want to ensure Redwood won’t store raw prompts beyond audit log necessity).
- Auth questions:
  1) If we go service-account + token exchange, what’s the recommended TTL for short-lived tokens? We prefer not to add an additional persistent credential store in devops.
  2) Does Redwood support OAuth client-credentials flow with automatic JWKS rotation?

We’ll loop in our infra lead (infra@ozarkdigital.com) for the deep-dive — preferred next week Tue/Wed mornings PST.

—Jessica

Subject: Fwd: Ozark Digital - internal notes on keying options (internal only)

Soojin / Ben — internal quick note before the deep-dive. Jessica’s questions are the right ones; here’s what I recommend we push as our standard:

- Short-lived tokens: 15–60 minute TTL depending on client risk profile. Recommend default 30 minutes. This pairs well with their preference to avoid extra persistent stores: they can use their existing token broker (e.g., an internal service that mints tokens) backed by their KMS.
- OAuth client credentials: Supported but requires additional setup on their side (registering OAuth client, JWKS endpoint). We do support automatic key rotation for our JWKS consumer, but they need to rotate the client secret and publish new JWKS when doing asymmetric keys.
- Service accounts pattern (recommended for prod):
   - Service account credential stored in KMS; exchange via token broker to short-lived token; token scoped to a specific model and route.
   - Enforce per-route quotas and token-scoped permissions (read-only embedding vs generation).
- Key rotation cadence: quarterly rotation for long-lived material; revoke and re-issue service account credential immediately if suspicious.

Also note: for rerankers, recommend routing embedding generation to the cheaper CPU-backed pool and reranker inference to the GPU pool; show them how to pin models to dedicated capacity later.

I added a short internal checklist (ozark-initial-map.md) to the attachments to guide the call.

—Marissa

Hi Jessica — great, thanks for the detail. Short answers to your auth questions and proposed agenda for the deep-dive: 

Auth answers:
- Recommended TTL: 30 minutes default. We’ve seen teams use 15m for high-risk endpoints (customer PII flows) and 60m for lower-risk backend batch jobs.
- OAuth / JWKS: Redwood supports OAuth client-credentials. We can validate JWTs against a customer-published JWKS; we also support rotating our public keys and can accept rotating client credentials. For ease-of-onboarding, service-account + token-broker is usually fastest for initial integration.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (60 mins):
1) 10m: architecture recap & compliance constraints (logs / retention)
2) 15m: auth & key management options (service accounts, OAuth, scoped API keys) + recommended defaults
3) 20m: routing & cost controls (region pinning, embedding vs reranker pools, batching)
4) 10m: SDK onboarding + sample token-broker walkthrough (we’ll step through integration-snippets.zip)
5) 5m: next steps & owners (who will send redlines / timeline)

I’ll send an invite for Tue 06 Jul 09:30 PST and Wed 07 Jul 09:30 PST — feel free to pick what works for your infra team and we’ll adjust.

Also re: logs/PII: we’ll document retention behavior and redact options in our SOC2 package; Marissa will include the short writeup in the deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward.

Soojin
